question: What is the minimum age to qualify for a Pennsylvania real estate broker's license?
explanation: Both RELRA Section 511(1) and 49 Pa. Code Section 35.271(a)(1) require a broker applicant to be at least 21 years of age, older than the 18-year minimum for a salesperson license under RELRA Section 521(1).
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.511(1); 49 Pa. Code Section 35.271(a)(1) (confirmed via legis.state.pa.us RELRA full text and pacodeandbulletin.gov)

question: How many years of experience as a licensed real estate salesperson (or equivalent) must a broker applicant have completed before taking the Pennsylvania broker examination?
explanation: RELRA Section 511(4) requires the applicant to have been engaged as a licensed real estate salesperson for at least three years, or to possess educational or experience qualifications the Commission deems equivalent -- confirmed identically in 49 Pa. Code Section 35.271(a)(3).
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.511(4); 49 Pa. Code Section 35.271(a)(3) (confirmed)

question: How many total hours (credits) of professional real estate education must a Pennsylvania broker applicant complete, absent a qualifying degree exemption?
explanation: RELRA Section 511(3) and 49 Pa. Code Section 35.271(a)(4) both require 240 hours, expressed by the Commission as 16 credits, of professional real estate instruction, roughly triple the 75-hour salesperson requirement.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.511(3); 49 Pa. Code Section 35.271(a)(4),(b) (confirmed)

question: Of the 16 required broker education credits, how many must specifically be in a Commission-developed or approved real estate LAW course?
choice_c: None -- law is not a mandatory subject
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.271(b)(2) requires 2 of the 16 credits to be in a Commission-developed or approved real estate LAW course, and separately requires 2 credits in a real estate OFFICE MANAGEMENT course -- the only two mandatory subject-specific credits in the broker curriculum.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.271(b)(2) (confirmed verbatim via pacodeandbulletin.gov)

question: Besides real estate law, which other subject is a mandatory 2-credit component of the Pennsylvania broker education requirement?
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.271(b)(2) mandates 2 credits in a Commission-developed or approved real estate office management course, alongside the 2-credit law course, before the candidate can round out the remaining 12 credits from a broader list of approved subjects.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.271(b)(2) (confirmed)

question: After the mandatory 2-credit law and 2-credit office management courses, how many of the remaining 12 broker education credits must come from at least 3 of the Commission's specifically enumerated subject list (e.g., real estate finance, investment, property management, valuation)?
explanation: Under 49 Pa. Code Section 35.271(b)(2), at least 6 of the remaining 12 credits must come from 3 or more of the enumerated courses (Real Estate Law, Real Estate Finance, Real Estate Investment, Residential/Nonresidential Property Management, Real Estate Sales, Residential Construction, and Valuation of Residential/Income-Producing Property); the final 6 credits may be any real estate courses.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.271(b)(2) (confirmed)

question: Which degree, standing alone, satisfies the Pennsylvania broker education requirement without the candidate having to show completion of specific coursework?
choice_a: An associate's degree in business administration
choice_b: A high school diploma with 5 years of unrelated work experience
choice_c: A juris doctor degree from an accredited law school
choice_d: A master's degree in any field
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.271(b)(1) deems a JD from an accredited law school (along with a bachelor's degree with a real estate major, or a bachelor's degree with equivalent real estate coursework) sufficient to satisfy the education requirement without further subject-specific proof.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.271(b)(1) (confirmed)

question: Within how many years prior to passing the broker licensing examination must a candidate's real estate education credits generally have been completed?
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.271(b)(5) requires that courses be completed within 10 years prior to the date of successful completion of the licensing examination.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.271(b)(5) (confirmed)

question: In Bhala v. State Real Estate Commission (Pa. Cmwlth. 1992), what did the Commonwealth Court hold regarding a salesperson's eligibility to sit for the broker examination?
choice_a: Merely holding a salesperson's license for 3 or more years, without more, does not by itself entitle a person to sit for the broker examination
choice_b: Any licensed salesperson may sit for the broker exam regardless of years held
choice_c: A salesperson license automatically converts to a broker license after 3 years
choice_d: The Commission may never deny a broker exam application from a licensed salesperson
explanation: In Bhala, the Commonwealth Court held that the mere possession of a salesperson's license for three or more years does not, standing alone, satisfy the experience requirement to sit for the broker's examination -- the Commission may still evaluate the substance of the applicant's actual real estate experience.
source_note: Bhala v. State Real Estate Commission, 617 A.2d 841 (Pa. Cmwlth. 1992), cited in Notes of Decisions to 49 Pa. Code Section 35.271 (confirmed via pacodeandbulletin.gov)

question: Which entity currently administers Pennsylvania's real estate broker and salesperson licensing examinations under contract with the State Real Estate Commission?
choice_d: The Pennsylvania Department of State directly, with no third-party vendor
explanation: Pearson VUE has administered Pennsylvania's real estate examination program since April 1, 2023, when PSI Exams ceased registering or administering PA real estate candidates (per the Commission's own announcement); the March 2026 Pearson VUE Pennsylvania Real Estate Commission Candidate Handbook confirms Pearson VUE as the current contracted vendor.
source_note: pa.gov Real Estate Commission Announcements page (confirmed: PSI-to-Pearson VUE transition effective April 1, 2023); Pearson VUE Pennsylvania Real Estate Commission Candidate Handbook #093900, rev. 03/2026 (confirmed vendor and effective handbook)

question: How many scored questions make up the national/general portion of the Pennsylvania broker examination?
explanation: The Pearson VUE candidate handbook's 'Available Exams and Time Allotted' table lists the Broker - National exam at 80 scored questions (plus 5 to 10 unscored pretest items), separate from the 40-question PA State-specific portion.
source_note: Pearson VUE Pennsylvania Real Estate Commission Candidate Handbook #093900, rev. 03/2026, 'Available Exams and Time Allotted' table (confirmed directly from the official PDF, extracted via pdftotext)

question: How many scored questions make up the Pennsylvania state-specific portion of the broker examination?
explanation: The candidate handbook confirms the Broker - PA State-specific exam consists of 40 scored questions (plus up to 10 unscored pretest items), for a combined total of 120 scored questions across both portions of the broker exam.
source_note: Pearson VUE Pennsylvania Real Estate Commission Candidate Handbook #093900, rev. 03/2026, 'Available Exams and Time Allotted' table; Pennsylvania Real Estate Broker Licensing Examination Content Outline, effective March 16, 2026 (both confirmed)

question: What is the minimum passing score required on each portion (national and state-specific) of the Pennsylvania broker examination?
explanation: The candidate handbook's exam table lists a 75% minimum passing score for both the Broker - National and Broker - PA State-specific portions -- a candidate must pass each portion independently.
source_note: Pearson VUE Pennsylvania Real Estate Commission Candidate Handbook #093900, rev. 03/2026, 'Available Exams and Time Allotted' table (confirmed)

question: How much time is allotted for the national portion of the Pennsylvania broker exam, and how much for the state-specific portion?
choice_a: 120 minutes for the national portion; 90 minutes for the state-specific portion
choice_b: 150 minutes for the national portion; 60 minutes for the state-specific portion
choice_d: 60 minutes for the national portion; 150 minutes for the state-specific portion
explanation: The candidate handbook's time-allotted column gives 150 minutes (2.5 hours) for the 80-question national portion and 60 minutes for the 40-question PA state-specific portion, totaling 210 minutes (3.5 hours) if both are taken.
source_note: Pearson VUE Pennsylvania Real Estate Commission Candidate Handbook #093900, rev. 03/2026, 'Available Exams and Time Allotted' table (confirmed)

question: What are the separate exam fees for the national and PA state-specific portions of the broker examination?
choice_a: $100 for the national portion; $100 for the state-specific portion
choice_b: $40 for the national portion; $40 for the state-specific portion
choice_c: $52 for the national portion; $49 for the state-specific portion
choice_d: $75 for the national portion; $25 for the state-specific portion
explanation: The candidate handbook's fee table lists $52 for the Broker - National exam and $49 for the Broker - PA State-specific exam; scheduling both on the same order qualifies the candidate for a combination discount, but scheduling them on separate orders requires paying each fee in full.
source_note: Pearson VUE Pennsylvania Real Estate Commission Candidate Handbook #093900, rev. 03/2026, 'Available Exams and Time Allotted' table (confirmed)

question: For how many years after passing the broker exam authorization (i.e., after completing the first required education course) may a candidate use that authorization to sit for the broker exam?
explanation: The candidate handbook states that broker candidates have a 10-year authorization period after passing the first education course to take their exams, twice the 5-year authorization period afforded to salesperson candidates.
source_note: Pearson VUE Pennsylvania Real Estate Commission Candidate Handbook #093900, rev. 03/2026, 'Retaking the Exam' section (confirmed)

question: Once a candidate passes both portions of the broker exam, for how long does that passing result remain valid for purposes of submitting a license application?
choice_a: 3 years from the date of passing
choice_b: 1 year from the date of passing
choice_c: 5 years from the date of passing
explanation: The candidate handbook and RELRA Section 512(c) both confirm exam results are valid for 3 years; if the two portions are passed on different dates, the 3-year window runs from the date the first portion was passed, and the completed application, fees, and documentation must reach the Commission within that window.
source_note: Pearson VUE Pennsylvania Real Estate Commission Candidate Handbook #093900, rev. 03/2026 (confirmed); 63 P.S. Section 455.512(c) (confirmed)

question: How is a Pennsylvania 'associate broker' defined under 49 Pa. Code Section 35.201?
choice_a: A salesperson with fewer than 3 years of experience
choice_b: An individual broker who is employed by another broker
choice_c: An unlicensed office manager who supervises paperwork only
choice_d: A broker who works exclusively in commercial transactions
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.201 defines an 'associate broker' simply as an individual broker who is employed by another broker -- meaning the person has met all broker-level qualifications but works under a supervising broker rather than operating independently, similar in concept to other states' associate-broker tiers.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.201 (Definitions) (confirmed verbatim via pacodeandbulletin.gov)

question: How is a 'broker of record' defined for a partnership, association, or corporation holding a Pennsylvania broker's license?
choice_a: Any salesperson designated by majority vote of the firm's agents
choice_b: The entity's registered agent for service of process, regardless of licensure
choice_c: The individual broker responsible for the real estate transactions of the entity
choice_d: The firm's highest-producing salesperson each calendar year
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.201 defines 'broker of record' as the individual broker responsible for the real estate transactions of a partnership, association, or corporation holding a broker's license; RELRA Section 513 requires that individual to independently meet the broker qualification and application requirements of Sections 511-512.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.201 (Definitions); 63 P.S. Section 455.513 (both confirmed)

question: A reciprocal salesperson or broker licensee from another state who wants to convert to a standard Pennsylvania license generally must do what?
choice_a: Retake both the national and state-specific portions from scratch
choice_b: Complete no additional exam, only pay a conversion fee
choice_c: Wait 5 years before becoming eligible to convert
choice_d: Pass only the Pennsylvania state-specific portion of the exam
explanation: The candidate handbook and 49 Pa. Code Section 35.271(c) both confirm that a reciprocal licensee converting to a standard license is exempt from the general exam-eligibility requirements and need only pass the state-specific portion of the applicable examination.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.271(c) (confirmed); Pearson VUE Pennsylvania Real Estate Commission Candidate Handbook #093900, rev. 03/2026 (confirmed)
